color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the problem
agent needs a policy / claim / plate number.
Spoken digits over a mobile are the WORST case:
short, phonetically confusable, no linguistic
context for a human or a model to lean on.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
today: 'ขอโทษค่ะ ทวนอีกครั้งได้ไหมคะ'
= dead air, the exact thing this product exists to remove

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.b: D43: the keypad stays live for the WHOLE call

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
agent clicks a labelled request
e.g. 'policy number'

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
a field appears on the workstation
AND a prompt for the caller

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: caller TYPES it. Digits land as they are pressed.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 47, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
do we already hold
this customer data?

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: check it against their ACTUAL policies

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
assurance promotes automatically
audit line: matched MT-2025-004512 at 14:32:07
stronger than an agent judging a spoken answer

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
recorded as a failed challenge.
Disclosure stays locked.

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: just accurate data entry - still a win

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
never capture a full secret.
Last 4 of a citizen id, never the whole number.
Never a card number. For secret-ish challenges store
THE OUTCOME ONLY - matched / not - never the digits.
A policy number is not a secret and is stored.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
P5 gotcha: the caller channel must STAY in the
Stasis app and be bridged from within it, or Asterisk
stops emitting ChannelDtmfReceived once bridged.
Always-on passive capture - no mode switch.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
same principle as D37. The keypad is the reliable
channel, the microphone is the lossy one. Give the
keypad the job speech is worst at. Needs no AI,
so it cannot degrade with one.
